evidence_boundaries: The cone-guided proton result is an author EPOCH 2D/3D PIC and ballistic-propagation study, not a proton-beam experiment; the reported 63% energy-spread and 46% focal-radius improvements are relative to the selected simulated planar baseline.

The radiative-turbulence PRD is a 2D decaying weakly excited electron-positron EPOCH study; its pitch-angle exponents are model-dependent and have no direct observation or laboratory validation in the paper.
PhySKIP accelerates a 1D drift-diffusion-Poisson nitrogen-discharge solver, not PIC; the 4.70x maximum uses one logical CPU and excludes loading and diagnostic output.
The PhySKIP development cases contributed to checkpoint selection, and its 500 ns completion tests are not a general long-time stability proof.
No EPOCH, PASCHEN-1D, CNN training, particle phase-space reconstruction, detector response, or experimental analysis was rerun locally.
